label: L1 a copy too busy to answer is taken for one that crashed, and its library taken over
L2 closing a copy removes the lock whoever it belongs to
L3 the copy the window started never gives the library up when it exits
L4 the lock is written over and not claimed by creating it, so a second copy simply takes it
L5 a stale lock is removed without reading it again, so a lock another copy took a moment earlier is removed
L6 a refused copy still answers the app's requests, and reads and writes the library
from: if (url.pathname.startsWith("/api/") || url.pathname.startsWith("/files/")) throw new HttpError(423, IN_USE_MESSAGE);

label: L7 the holder's answers carry no id, so every other copy takes it for a dead one
L8 any program that answers on the old port is taken for the holder
L9 a refused connection is taken for a busy copy, so a crashed copy's lock is never taken over
L10 Try again is a change that does not need the app's own header

label: L11 Try again never claims the library, so the refused copy stays refused after the other closes
L12 closing a copy keeps the lock, so the next copy is refused until it times out
